newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares ride to near highs, Ericsson falls.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares ride to near highs, Ericsson falls.

text.p: Swedish share prices rode on optimism sparked by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's forecast for moderate U.S. growth amid low inflation with other European markets to end near an all-time high on Wednesday.
The general index ended up 1.06 percent at 3,172.89. Shares totalling a healthy five billion crowns changed owners.
Players traded shares in telecoms group Ericsson up six crowns but then got cold feet ahead of first half results due by 0900 GMT on Thursday. The share ended at 329 crowns, down one.
Analysts expect Ericsson to post a 21 percent rise in pre-tax profits at 5.11 billion crowns.
"One could argue that at these levels it's fully-valued. But in these markets, who can say? asked Morgan Stanley analyst Angela Dean, before the share started to back down.
Volvo advanced six crowns to 219. The share has jumped from 204 crowns shortly before it reported solid first half profits on Tuesday.

Rollerbearing maker SKF rallied 12 crowns but ended at 232, up two. "Merrill Lynch upgraded SKF to increase from neutral. In addition, its rival Timken came out with strong half-year results," one broker said.
